title: Nonclassicality from Incomplete Fock-State Statistics
authors: Martin Žonda, Pavel Baláž, Lukáš Lachman, Darren W. Moore, Tomáš Novotný, Radim Filip
abstract: Nonclassicality in bosonic systems can be certified directly from occupation probabilities without full state reconstruction. To complete a library of such criteria we introduce a numerical framework that constructs optimal linear nonclassicality witnesses from arbitrary subsets of measured occupation probabilities by solving a semi-infinite linear program. The method contains known analytical criteria as special cases while generally detecting substantially larger nonclassical regions. We provide an open-source implementation of the numerical optimization together with the analytical criteria discussed here, enabling direct application of the framework to measured occupation statistics across bosonic platforms. As a case study, we apply it to the resonant Jaynes--Cummings model with thermal states and reveal nonclassicality at short interaction times and close to thermal balance, where detection of nonclassicality is otherwise challenging.
summary: This paper introduces a general numerical framework to certify quantum nonclassicality in bosonic systems directly from partial measurements of photon occupation probabilities. By solving a semi-infinite linear program, the authors construct optimal witnesses that surpass the detection limits of existing analytical criteria. The method is successfully applied to the Jaynes-Cummings model, revealing previously undetected nonclassical behavior near thermal equilibrium.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of certifying quantum nonclassicality in bosonic systems using only incomplete measurements of occupation probabilities, thereby avoiding the need for full state reconstruction.
main_result: The developed numerical framework successfully constructs optimal linear nonclassicality witnesses that generally detect larger nonclassical regions than existing analytical criteria. This was demonstrated in a case study on the Jaynes-Cummings model, revealing nonclassicality near thermal equilibrium.
method: The core method involves formulating the nonclassicality certification as solving a semi-infinite linear program, which is solved numerically using an iterative cutting-plane procedure.
model_or_system: The primary physical system studied is bosonic systems, with a detailed case study applied to the resonant Jaynes-Cummings (JC) model involving a qubit and a bosonic mode. Another test case involves probabilistic boson addition to a coherent state.
key_observables: Occupation probabilities of Fock states ($P_k$), and the resulting nonclassicality witness function $W(\lambda; \mathbf{P})$.
important_parameters: Interaction time ($	au$), initial excited-state population ($p_e$), and the number of measured probabilities ($N_P$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that nonclassicality can be detected if the measured probability vector cannot be expressed as a convex combination of Poisson distributions (coherent states).
figures_summary: Figures map out nonclassicality regions in parameter spaces (e.g., $p_e$ vs $N_P$ for the JC model), comparing the detection boundaries found by the general numerical criterion against those from specific analytical witnesses.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general mathematical framework using linear programming to define the witness. It then compares this general numerical approach against known analytical criteria (Klyshko, Counting Matrix). Finally, it applies the method to the JC model and boson addition to demonstrate its superior detection capability in specific physical regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general computational tool for quantum optics and AMO physics, allowing researchers to map out nonclassical regimes in complex open quantum systems (like the JC model) where traditional analytical bounds fail or are incomplete.
